sections.heading: AIM
sections.paragraph: To implement K-Means clustering on the UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones dataset, determine the optimal number of clusters using the elbow method, evaluate clustering quality using silhouette scores, visualize clusters via PCA, and align cluster labels with true activity labels for interpretation.

plots.caption: Elbow method and Silhouette scores across k = 2 to 10
PCA 2D visualization of K-Means clusters on HAR sensor data
Cluster vs true activity alignment using confusion matrix heatmap

rows: Loaded 7352 training and 2947 test samples with 561 features; scaled with StandardScaler
Determine optimal k via elbow method
Computed inertia and silhouette scores for k = 2..10; identified k = 6 as best trade-off
Fit K-Means on training data; inertia = {inertia:.2f}; silhouette score = {silhouette:.4f}
Clusters assigned for train and test sets
Reduced 561 features to 2 principal components; plotted clusters vs true activities
Visual separation observed with some overlap
Used Hungarian algorithm to map 6 cluster IDs to 6 true activity labels
Documented metrics, analyzed bias-variance tradeoff, and identified future improvements (t-SNE/UMAP)
Report compiled and ready for upload

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: Applied K-Means clustering to a real-world sensor-based activity dataset
Used the elbow method and silhouette analysis to choose the number of clusters
Visualized high-dimensional data via PCA and interpreted cluster separation
Aligned unsupervised cluster labels with supervised activity labels using a combinatorial assignment
Built intuition for the limitations of distance-based clustering in high dimensions and explored advanced visualizations (t-SNE/UMAP) as next steps
